chapter: Dave Bartholomew band and early recording
title: Death of his first wife and mother in 1951
summary: His wife, who had a heart condition, dropped dead near his mother's house and the shock killed his mother; Earl Palmer pulled him back to the club.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Now, you had... Now, you said you were married then. Did you have any kids?
And in 1951, the lady I married, I said they had the same name as my mother. Yeah. So she became a Leona Tyler also.

And as a child, she had rheumatic fever that it messed up her heart. Why? And in 1951, she was going to visit my mom and she got two doors from my mom's house and she was... My mom was sitting outside and saw my wife coming and my wife dropped dead and the shock from her killed my mother.
Oh, great. Perfect. So that was in 1951?
So how did that affect you at that point?
Well, it broke me up. I mean, my mother and my wife at the same time. Right. You know, it did. But I got through it.
Did you stop playing for a while? No.

I was no longer with Dave's band and I recall that Earl Palmer, we were really close then and when they died that week and he said, man, it's no sense in you just sitting down and you're sorry. Just come on to the club, you know, at San Jacinto. Yeah. And they were playing and I just, you know, went there. No, I didn't sit down. Just went to...
Just to get away from my sorrow.
Oh, yeah. So it took you X amount of some time to get over? Well, yeah. You went through it.
Yeah, it took time. It took time, but I mean, I still played, you know. Mm-hmm.
